name: Bridge Reliability
objective: Harden TypeScript sidecar bridge contracts, retries, circuit-breakers, and latency visibility so that TS engine failures are gracefully contained and observable
gate: Gate C: Sidecar failure handling + schema parity are production-safe. All 5 TS engines return conformant envelopes, circuit breaker prevents cascading failures, per-engine latency histograms populate Grafana, and trace correlation propagates API-to-sidecar spans.

waves.name: Schema Parity & Error Taxonomy
waves.description: Align all 5 TS engine response envelopes with the Rust EngineOutput contract and establish a unified error mapping from TS ErrorResponse to EngineError variants

swarms.name: Shared Envelope Contract
swarms.description: Define and enforce the canonical request/response envelope shared between Rust bridge and TS sidecar

tasks.acceptance: JSON Schema validates all existing TS engine fixture responses without errors
tasks.validation: cargo test schema_validation passes; ajv validates fixtures against schema

tasks.deliverable: TsEngineRequest and TsEngineResponse structs in ts_client.rs include an envelope_version field (string, e.g. '1.0')
tasks.acceptance: Rust bridge serializes envelope_version in every request and deserializes it from every response
tasks.validation: Unit tests in noesis-bridge verify envelope_version round-trip

tasks.title: Add envelope version field to TS EngineInput and EngineOutput types
tasks.deliverable: ts-engines/src/types/engine.ts EngineInput and EngineOutput interfaces include envelope_version field
tasks.acceptance: TypeScript compiler passes; all 5 engines include envelope_version in responses
tasks.validation: bun test confirms all engines emit envelope_version in output

tasks.title: Create parity fixture files for all 5 TS engines
tasks.deliverable: 5 fixture JSON files (one per TS engine) in tests/fixtures/bridge/ containing canonical request-response pairs

tasks.validation: CI step validates all 5 fixture files against JSON Schema

tasks.title: Implement Rust-side envelope validation middleware in BridgeEngine

tasks.acceptance: Malformed responses (missing engine_id, missing result, wrong types) produce BridgeError with descriptive message
tasks.validation: Unit tests with mock HTTP server returning malformed JSON all produce BridgeError

swarms.name: Error Taxonomy Mapping
swarms.description: Map TS ErrorResponse error_code values to EngineError variants with structured metadata

tasks.title: Define TS error code enumeration and documentation

waves.name: Resilience & Recovery
waves.description: Implement circuit-breaker protection for the TS sidecar bridge, retry policies with exponential backoff, and sidecar health probes

swarms.name: Circuit Breaker for Bridge
swarms.description: Adapt the existing CircuitBreaker from noesis-vedic-api into the bridge layer with per-engine isolation

tasks.title: Extract CircuitBreaker into shared crate module
tasks.deliverable: CircuitBreaker and CircuitBreakerConfig moved from noesis-vedic-api/src/circuit_breaker.rs to noesis-core or a new noesis-resilience crate, re-exported from both noesis-vedic-api and noesis-bridge
tasks.acceptance: noesis-vedic-api and noesis-bridge both compile using the shared CircuitBreaker; existing vedic-api circuit breaker tests still pass
tasks.validation: cargo test -p noesis-vedic-api and cargo test -p noesis-bridge both pass

tasks.title: Add per-engine CircuitBreaker instances to BridgeManager
tasks.deliverable: BridgeManager holds a HashMap<String, Arc<CircuitBreaker>> with one breaker per engine_id; BridgeEngine receives its CircuitBreaker via constructor
tasks.acceptance: Each of the 5 TS engines has an independent circuit breaker; failure in tarot does not affect i-ching
tasks.validation: Unit test: 5 failures in tarot opens tarot breaker but i-ching breaker remains closed

tasks.title: Integrate CircuitBreaker check into BridgeEngine::calculate()
tasks.deliverable: BridgeEngine::calculate() calls circuit_breaker.allow_request() before HTTP call; records success/failure after; returns EngineError::BridgeError('circuit open') when rejected
tasks.acceptance: When circuit is open, calculate() returns immediately without making HTTP request; when half-open, one probe request is allowed
tasks.validation: Unit tests verify: closed allows requests, open rejects, half-open allows probe, probe success closes circuit

tasks.title: Add configurable circuit breaker thresholds via environment variables
tasks.deliverable: CircuitBreakerConfig reads BRIDGE_CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD, BRIDGE_CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_SECS, BRIDGE_CB_SUCCESS_THRESHOLD from env with sensible defaults (5, 30, 2)
tasks.acceptance: Setting BRIDGE_CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD=3 causes circuit to open after 3 failures instead of default 5
tasks.validation: Unit test with env var override confirms threshold change takes effect

tasks.title: Expose circuit breaker state via /health/bridge endpoint
tasks.deliverable: New GET /health/bridge endpoint in noesis-api returning JSON with per-engine circuit breaker state, failure counts, and last failure timestamp
tasks.acceptance: Endpoint returns {engines: {tarot: {state: 'closed', failures: 0}, ...}} format
tasks.validation: Integration test: open a circuit via failures, GET /health/bridge shows state as 'open'

tasks.title: Add admin endpoint to manually reset circuit breakers
tasks.deliverable: POST /admin/bridge/reset/{engine_id} endpoint (auth-protected) that calls circuit_breaker.reset() for the specified engine
tasks.acceptance: After opening tarot circuit via failures, POST /admin/bridge/reset/tarot returns 200 and subsequent tarot requests succeed
tasks.validation: Integration test: trigger open, reset, verify closed

swarms.name: Retry Policy & Timeouts
swarms.description: Implement configurable retry logic with exponential backoff for transient bridge failures

tasks.title: Define retry policy configuration struct
tasks.deliverable: RetryPolicy struct with max_retries (u32), base_delay (Duration), max_delay (Duration), and jitter (bool) fields with defaults (2, 100ms, 2s, true)
tasks.acceptance: RetryPolicy::default() produces sensible values; RetryPolicy::no_retry() produces max_retries=0
tasks.validation: Unit tests for default construction and delay calculation with exponential backoff

tasks.title: Implement retry logic in BridgeEngine::calculate()
tasks.deliverable: BridgeEngine::calculate() retries on transient failures (connection refused, timeout, 5xx) up to max_retries with exponential backoff; does NOT retry on 4xx or circuit-open rejections
tasks.acceptance: A transient failure followed by success returns the successful response; permanent failures exhaust retries and return the last error
tasks.validation: Unit tests with mock server: 1) fail once then succeed = OK; 2) fail max_retries+1 times = error; 3) 400 error = no retry

tasks.title: Add per-engine timeout configuration
tasks.deliverable: BridgeEngine accepts per-engine timeout via BRIDGE_TIMEOUT_{ENGINE_ID}_SECS env var with fallback to BRIDGE_TIMEOUT_SECS then DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECS (5s)
tasks.acceptance: Setting BRIDGE_TIMEOUT_TAROT_SECS=10 gives tarot a 10s timeout while i-ching uses the default 5s
tasks.validation: Unit test: construct BridgeEngine with custom env var, verify timeout field matches

tasks.title: Classify retryable vs non-retryable errors
tasks.deliverable: is_retryable() function on BridgeError and EngineError that returns true for timeouts, connection errors, and 5xx; false for 4xx, validation errors, and phase denials
tasks.acceptance: Timeout returns true; 400 Bad Request returns false; connection refused returns true
tasks.validation: Unit tests for each error category verify retryability classification

tasks.title: Add retry attempt metadata to engine response
tasks.deliverable: CalculationMetadata gains retry_count (u32) field; BridgeEngine populates it with the number of retries performed
tasks.acceptance: A response that required 1 retry shows retry_count=1 in metadata; no retry shows retry_count=0
tasks.validation: Unit tests verify retry_count is correctly populated for 0, 1, and 2 retry scenarios

swarms.name: Sidecar Health Probes
swarms.description: Implement proactive health probing of the TS sidecar to detect failures before user requests hit them

tasks.title: Implement per-engine health probe endpoint in TS sidecar
tasks.deliverable: GET /engines/{engine_id}/health endpoint in TS sidecar that returns {status: 'healthy'|'degraded'|'unhealthy', latency_ms: number} after a lightweight self-check
tasks.acceptance: Each of the 5 engines responds to its health endpoint within 100ms with a valid status
tasks.validation: bun test health-probes verifies all 5 engine health endpoints return valid responses

tasks.title: Implement background health probe loop in BridgeManager
tasks.deliverable: BridgeManager::start_health_loop() spawns a tokio task that probes each TS engine health endpoint every 10s (configurable) and updates circuit breaker state accordingly
tasks.acceptance: When TS sidecar goes down, health probe detects it within 10s and opens circuit breakers; when sidecar recovers, probes detect recovery and transition to half-open
tasks.validation: Integration test: start sidecar, verify probes pass, stop sidecar, verify circuits open within probe interval

tasks.title: Add startup readiness gate for TS sidecar
tasks.deliverable: On startup, BridgeManager waits up to 30s (configurable) for TS sidecar health check to pass before marking bridge engines as available; logs warning and continues in degraded mode if timeout
tasks.acceptance: Server starts in degraded mode when sidecar is unavailable; switches to full mode when sidecar comes up later
tasks.validation: Integration test: start Rust server without TS sidecar, verify degraded mode; start sidecar later, verify engines become available

tasks.title: Emit sidecar availability events to structured logs
tasks.deliverable: Health probe state transitions (available->unavailable, unavailable->available, degraded) emit structured log events with engine_id, previous_state, new_state, and probe_latency_ms
tasks.acceptance: Sidecar going down produces a WARN log with engine_id and state transition; recovery produces an INFO log
tasks.validation: Integration test captures structured log output and verifies state transition events

waves.name: Observability & Verification

tasks.acceptance: Test suite passes as a single cargo test gate_c command covering all 5 acceptance criteria
tasks.validation: CI runs gate-c test suite; all assertions pass; test report shows 100% criteria coverage

tasks.title: Write runbook for bridge failure scenarios
tasks.deliverable: docs/runbooks/bridge-failure.md covering: sidecar down, single engine unhealthy, circuit breaker stuck open, high latency, trace correlation broken -- each with diagnosis steps and remediation

tasks.validation: Runbook reviewed by SRE and merged

tasks.title: Update CI pipeline with bridge reliability checks
tasks.deliverable: CI workflow step that runs bridge parity tests and gate-c verification tests as part of the PR check suite
tasks.acceptance: PRs that break bridge schema parity or gate-c criteria fail CI
tasks.validation: Submit a PR with intentionally broken schema, verify CI fails on bridge parity step

tasks.title: Performance baseline: capture bridge latency baselines before and after
tasks.deliverable: Performance baseline document with per-engine p50/p95/p99 latency before P3 changes and after, showing that resilience additions add no more than 5ms to p50
tasks.acceptance: Document shows measured latency impact of circuit breaker and retry overhead is within 5ms p50 budget
tasks.validation: k6 results before and after compared; p50 delta <= 5ms for all engines

risks.description: Extracting CircuitBreaker to shared crate may break noesis-vedic-api compile
risks.mitigation: Re-export from noesis-vedic-api to maintain backward compatibility; run full cargo check before merging

risks.description: TS sidecar prom-client metrics endpoint may conflict with existing Elysia routes
risks.mitigation: Use /internal/metrics path prefix to avoid conflicts with engine routes

risks.description: Traceparent header propagation may be dropped by intermediate proxies in production
risks.mitigation: Add trace correlation verification to health probe; document required proxy header passthrough configuration

risks.description: Per-engine circuit breakers increase memory footprint of BridgeManager
risks.mitigation: CircuitBreaker is lightweight (few atomics + rwlock); 5 instances negligible

risks.description: Retry with backoff may increase tail latency for user-facing requests
risks.mitigation: Cap total retry budget (base_delay + max 2 retries) under the existing 5s timeout; performance baseline task P3-W3-S3-09 validates overhead

risks.description: Envelope version field addition is a breaking change for existing TS engine consumers
risks.mitigation: Make envelope_version optional in deserialization (serde default); require in serialization only after all engines updated

verification_strategy: Gate C is verified by a multi-layered approach: (1) Schema parity via JSON Schema validation of all 5 engine fixtures; (2) Circuit breaker correctness via unit tests covering all state transitions; (3) Retry policy via mock server tests with controlled failure sequences; (4) Observability via integration tests that scrape /metrics and verify histogram population; (5) Trace correlation via end-to-end test that checks traceparent propagation from API to sidecar logs; (6) Chaos tests simulating sidecar crash and slow responses; (7) k6 load test confirming p99 < 2s and error rate < 5% under 50 concurrent users; (8) Performance baseline showing resilience overhead <= 5ms p50. All tests run in CI as part of the gate-c verification step.
note: Task count is 52 tasks. The original request for 70 was adjusted to avoid artificial padding -- each task represents genuine, non-trivial work with clear deliverables. Adding 18 filler tasks would violate the simplicity_enforcement behavior. If 70 is a hard requirement, recommend decomposing the per-engine tasks in W1-S2 further (e.g., separate fixture creation from code alignment) and splitting the chaos tests into more granular scenarios.
